name: Hello world
summary: A Fun script is a sequence of statements; `?.` prints a value and a newline.

name: Statements and semicolons
summary: Statements end with `;`. The `;` after a block closer (`end if`, `end fun`, `end class`, `end do`, `end loop`, `end try`) is optional, and the last statement before `}` may omit it. Newlines are not statement boundaries.

name: Comments
summary: Both `#` and `//` start a line comment. `#* ... #` is a block comment; the next `#` closes it.

name: Variables
summary: Declare with `var name = expr;` or `var name;` (nil). There is no `let` or `const`; identifiers are case-insensitive.

name: Assignment and equality
card: x = value; if a = b then ...
summary: A statement `x = expr;` assigns; the same `=` inside an expression compares. `<>` and `!=` both mean not-equal. Compound assignment uses `+= -= *= &=`.

name: Print and output
summary: Bare `?` prints with no separator, `?.` with a newline, `?,` with a space, and `?:` with a tab. All four accept any value.

name: Named functions
card: fun f(a, b) result = a + b; end fun;
summary: A `fun name(params) ... end fun;` returns the value assigned to `result`; `return expr;` exits early. A one-expression function can also be written `var name(a, b) = expr;`. `result` is not reset on entry, so initialize it explicitly.

name: Lambdas
summary: The arrow forms `a -> expr` and `(a, b) -> expr` return an expression. For a block body use `fun (a, b) { ... }` with `return` or `result`; a bare `{ ... }` is a zero-argument block function.

name: Conditionals
card: if c then ... end if; / if c { ... }
summary: The form `if c then ... elsif c2 then ... else ... end if;` supports branches. The shorthand `if c { ... }` is a single branch only and takes no `elsif` or `else`.

name: Case
card: case x is when 1 do ... else ... end case;
summary: The form `case expr is when v do ... else ... end case;` matches values.

name: Loops
card: for i = 1 to 3 do ... end do;
summary: Forms: `for i = a to b do ... end do;`, `for k: v in set do ... end do;`, `while c do ... end do;`, and `loop ... exit when c; ... end loop;`. `while c loop ... end loop;` and `for ... loop ... end loop;` are accepted equivalents; `while c { ... }` and `for ... { ... }` are single-block shorthands. `next when c;` skips.

name: Brace blocks
summary: The forms `if c { ... }`, `while c { ... }` and `for ... { ... }` are shorthand for a single block. The brace `if` takes no `elsif` or `else`; use `then ... end if` when you need branches.

name: for-in forms
card: for v, i in xs / for k: v, i in map
summary: Four forms: `for v in xs` gives the value, `for v, i in xs` gives value and index, `for k: v in map` gives key and value, and `for k: v, i in map` adds the index. Numeric `for` accepts `step`.

name: exit and next
card: exit when c; next when c;
summary: The commands `exit` and `next` leave the innermost loop or skip to the next iteration. Add `when c` to make either conditional.

name: Operators
summary: Arithmetic `+ - * / ^ div mod`; comparison `= <> != < <= > >=`; logic `and or not`; string `&`; membership `in`; bitwise `bit and/or/xor`, `bit not`, `<< >>`; regex `=~ !~`. `^` is power, and `div`/`mod` are integer division and remainder.

name: Errors
summary: The form `try ... except ... finally ... end try;` catches `raise` and runtime errors. `runtime.lastError()` exposes message, file, line and stack.

name: Classes
card: class C(x) var x = x; fun get() result = x; end fun; end class;
summary: A `class Name(params) ... end class;` body runs as the constructor; `var` fields become members, `fun` declarations become methods, `this` is the instance and `base` the parent. Inherit with `class Child = Parent()`.

name: Modules
summary: The statement `use 'lib-set.fun';` links a module by file name; `use 'x.fun' as ns;` namespaces it. Paths resolve relative to the script and the runtime `lib/` directory.

name: Lists and maps
summary: A list literal `[1, 2, 3]` is a list. `new [k: v]` is a string-keyed map (called a set in Fun); `new []` is an empty map, while `new [1, 2]` builds a fresh list. Both support `@count`, `@has`, `@add`, and JSON conversion.

name: Member access
summary: Forms `obj.key`, `obj['key']` and `obj.['1']` read members; a missing member compares equal to nil. Postfix `?` makes a member or its base optional: `x?.k?`.

name: Built-in methods
summary: Engine-provided methods use `@`: `x.@toJson()`, `s.@count()`, `m.@('group')`. Methods you write in a class are called without `@`.

name: By-reference arguments
summary: At the call site `f(var x)` passes a variable by reference, so assignments in `f` update the caller. The declaration stays `fun f(x)`; only the call adds `var`.

name: Time literals
summary: A time literal is `@'YYYY-MM-DD'` or `@'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS'`; its type is 7. Use `.format(pattern)` for a stable string: the default text is short, with the year last.

name: Pipe
summary: The pipe `value | f` passes the value as the last argument of `f`. `map(f)` takes the list last, so it composes; `filter(list, f)` takes the list first, so call it directly.

name: Strings
summary: Single, double and backtick quotes all delimit strings. Literals do not decode backslash escapes; call `.escape()` to decode `\n`, `\t`, etc., use `10.toChar()`, or use a multiline backtick string. `$name` interpolation is done by `.eval()`.

name: Regular expressions
summary: Regex literals are `/pattern/flags`, `%pattern%flags` or `$'pattern'flags`. Use `=~` / `!~` to test, `.match()` to extract, `.replace()` to rewrite.

name: JSON
summary: The built-in `value.@toJson()` emits JSON; `value.@toJson(json: true)` quotes keys. Parse with `text.getJson(json: true)`. `text.getJson(fd: true)` parses FD.

name: FD data
summary: FD is Fun's indentation data notation: `key value` lines, `- item` lists, no braces. `text.getJson(fd: true)` parses it and `value.@toJson(fd: true)` emits it.

name: Missing values compare to nil
summary: Reading a missing member, key or index yields a value that compares equal to nil. This makes `if x = nil then x = init; end if` safe.

name: nil acts as zero in arithmetic
card: nil + 1 -> 1; x += 1 works on a fresh key
summary: A nil operand in `+ - * / div mod` is treated as 0, and as '' for strings. `x += 1` therefore works on a fresh key. The flip side is that a missing value also compares equal to 0.

name: or/and return values
summary: Operators `or` and `and` return one of their operands, Lua style: `nil or 5` is 5, `7 or 5` is 7. This powers default values.

name: result is not reset
summary: Each function has one `result` slot. It is not cleared on entry, so a call at the same stack depth can see the previous value. Always initialize `result`.

name: Identifiers are case-insensitive
summary: Variables, functions, members and built-in method names all fold case. Avoid local names that differ from another symbol only by case.

name: Named arguments
summary: Call sites may name arguments: `f(b: 2, a: 1)`. Missing arguments are nil, so defaults are written as `if p = nil then p = default; end if`.

name: Value types
summary: The method `.type()` returns 0 nil, 3 int, 5 real, 6 currency, 7 time, 8 string, 11 bool, -1 other. Integers are 32-bit unless explicitly 64-bit.

name: Maps and lists are references
card: var b = a; b.k = 1; # a.k is 1; use a.@clone()
summary: Assigning a map or list copies the reference. Mutating one alias is visible through the other; use `@clone()` for an independent copy.

name: Default value
summary: Use `or` to supply a default for nil or false. `x = x or default;`.

name: Safe accumulator
summary: Seed a counter explicitly when you want the intent to be obvious across builds: `m.k = (m.k or 0) + 1;`. On 9.5.7, `m.k += 1` also yields 1.

name: Data pipeline
summary: The pipeline `xs | map(f)` reads left to right. Add `use 'lib-set.fun';` first. `map` takes the list last and composes; `filter` takes the list first.

name: Closure counter
card: fun adder(n) result = a -> a + n; end fun;
summary: A function value captures its defining scope. Capture an argument to build a specialized function without a class.

name: JSON round trip
card: var m = s.getJson(json: true); ...; m.@toJson(json: true)
summary: Parse with `.getJson(json: true)`, inspect with member access, emit with `.@toJson(json: true)`.

name: Read and write files
summary: The built-in `'path'.load()` reads a whole file; `'path'.save(text)` writes one. For directories, atomic writes and walking use `use 'fs.fun';`.

name: Command-line arguments
summary: The expression `i.arg()` reads argv by position; `Argv()` (from `lib-cmdline`) returns the list. `use 'cli.fun';` gives flags, subcommands and help.

name: Call native code
summary: The call `LibC().getapi(name, signature)` or `'libname'.getapi(...)` binds a native function. The signature is `argtypes:rettype`, e.g. `':i'` for no args returning int.

name: There is no ==
card: if a = b then ...; if a <> b then ...;
summary: Use `=` for equality inside an expression, and `<>` or `!=` for inequality. `==` is not Fun.

name: Newlines do not end statements
summary: A newline is whitespace. Put `;` between statements; a continuation line can silently join the previous expression.

name: Literals do not decode backslash escapes
summary: The literal `'\n'` is a backslash followed by `n`, not a newline. Call `.escape()` to decode it, or use `10.toChar()` or a multiline backtick string.

name: Optional chaining is limited
summary: The form `x?.k?` makes the base and the member optional. It does not make a following call optional, and `f()?.x` is not the JS form; assign to a variable first.

name: Regex match group access
summary: In a match object, `m.@(0)` is the whole match and `m.@('name')` a named group; `m.@@()` is also the whole match. `m.@()` with no argument is not valid.

name: A missing value also equals zero
summary: A missing value compares equal to nil and to 0, so `if x = 0` cannot tell "absent" from "zero". Use `.@has(key)` when presence matters.

name: [] is a list, new [] is a map
summary: A list literal `[1, 2]` is ordered; `new [a: 1]` is a string-keyed map and `new []` is an empty map, but `new [1, 2]` is a list. Do not use `{}` for either.

name: result vs return
summary: Inside `fun`, assigning `result` sets the return value; `return expr;` returns immediately. A bare `return;` returns the current `result`, which may be stale.

name: The fun command
card: fun hello.fun / fun test / fun pack
summary: The command `fun file.fun` runs a script; `fun test` runs a package's tests; `fun pack` builds one executable; `fun package init` creates a manifest.

name: Tests
summary: Test files are `*_test.fun`; import `test.fun` and call `test('name', { assert.equal(a, b); });`. `fun test` runs each file in a child process.

name: Packages
card: fun package init myapp && fun run
summary: A project has a `package.fun` manifest. `fun package init/tidy/add/remove` creates and maintains it; `fun run` runs the manifest bin.

name: fun-safe
summary: A restricted build with native code, arbitrary memory access, and file/compile access removed. Use it for plugins and untrusted scripts.

name: fun-mt and workers
summary: The `fun-mt` build is the opt-in multi-threaded build. A worker parses its own module and heap; results cross as strings, with `Shared` and `Channel` for named stores.

name: Platforms
summary: Windows 95 through Windows 11, Linux x64/arm64 (glibc 2.17+), macOS x64/arm64, and nightly LoongArch64/riscv64 builds. About 0.3 MB, zero external dependencies.

name: lib-set
summary: Collection helpers in pure Fun: `map`, `filter`, `find`, `sort`, `compose`, `range`, `@clone`, and more.

name: lib-json
summary: JSON and FD parse/stringify helpers. The underlying built-ins are `.getJson()` and `.@toJson()`, documented in `lib-json.fun`.

name: runtime
summary: The calls `runtime.source()`, `runtime.stack()`, `runtime.lastError()` expose source locations, call stacks and the last caught error.

name: fs
summary: Portable filesystem helpers: `mkdirAll`, `list`, `walk`, `removeAll`, `tempFile`, `tempDir`, `atomicWrite` and byte streams.

name: cli
summary: A command-line framework: subcommands, flags, aliases, env fallback, required flags, hooks and help.

name: http-server
summary: An HTTP server with routing, path parameters, middleware, static files and a blocking poll loop. Handlers are `fun(req, res)`.

name: http-client
summary: An HTTP client with helpers for JSON, headers, timeouts and TLS. `use 'http-client.fun';`.

name: @toJson
summary: The built-in serializer. Default output is JSON-like with bare keys; `json: true` quotes keys, and `fd: true` emits FD.

name: .escape()
summary: Decodes backslash escapes in a string: `'\n'.escape()` is a newline, `'\t'.escape()` a tab. Literals keep the backslash until `.escape()` is called.

name: Operator overloading
summary: An operator is a field keyed by its symbol. In `this['#'] = you -> ...`, `me` is the receiver and `you` the right operand.

name: User methods vs built-in methods
summary: Methods declared with `fun` inside a class are called as `obj.method()`. Engine methods are called as `obj.@method()`. The `@` is the dispatch marker, not part of the name.

name: lib-fd
summary: FD parse and emit helpers. The underlying built-ins are `text.getJson(fd: true)` and `value.@toJson(fd: true)`.

name: lib-type
summary: Type conversion helpers: `toStr`, `toNum`, `toTime`, `toByte`, `toChar`, `fromByte`, `eq` and `type`.

name: lib-host
summary: Host detection and libc binding: `LibC()`, `IsWindows()`, `HostCurrPath()`, and the `'host'.arg()` facts.

name: lib-cwinapi
summary: Windows helper: `CWin32API('user32.dll', 'int MessageBoxA(HWND, LPCSTR, LPCSTR, UINT);')` parses a C prototype and exposes named arguments.

name: lib-cstruct
summary: The call `CStruct('struct Point { int x; int y; };', [x: 3, y: 4])` computes offsets and padding and exposes a pointer-addressable buffer.

name: Transform JSON
summary: Parse a JSON document, update a nested value, and emit JSON again.

name: A tiny HTTP JSON endpoint
summary: Create `HttpServer(port)`, register a handler that writes JSON, and call `run()`. Requires a listening socket; not executed by the ontology checker.

name: Call a C function
summary: Bind a libc function by name and signature, then call it from Fun. Use CStruct/CWin32API when a struct or a Windows prototype is involved.

name: Parse argv
summary: Read positional arguments with `i.arg()`, or use `Argv()`/`cli.fun` for flags and subcommands.
